analysis.title: The Great Capital Squeeze Is Starting To Break Things
key_insights: European banks sold off sharply: SX7E traded down around 4% at the lows, closed well below the 100-day MA, with little support until the 200-day MA near the longer-term trend line. The note had flagged European banks as next after the US banks drop on Sep 30.

Italian and Spanish 10-year spreads versus France have collapsed and both now trade through zero, so France is the new periphery. TS Lombard sees another round of widening if budget negotiations fail to improve, with 200bp potentially in play.

France's private-sector debt burden is considerably higher than the US, while government debt is comparable to US levels. With public and private balance sheets both stretched, there is no easy adjustment path.
The CAC 40 weekly chart is at oversold levels reached only a handful of times in recent years, which makes a contrarian bounce case possible.

Privorotsky argues a global capital squeeze is developing: large sovereign financing needs plus AI-driven demand for capital (SpaceX reportedly seeking $40bn, Broadcom exploring more than $50bn) raise crowding-out risk and may explain why real yields refuse to fall.
Privorotsky sees two outcomes: AI becomes increasingly self-financing, or capital gets rationed elsewhere and weaker parts of the economy crack. CCC spreads may already be an early warning.
The US 10-year yield has moved closely with selected hyperscaler CDS spreads, linking the AI boom to rising financing costs and credit stress.

The US 30-year yield printed two shooting stars in a row near the upper end of a steep trend channel, well above the 21-day MA. A pullback is possible without breaking the uptrend, pending a confirmation candle.

JPM says CTA momentum signals in US Treasuries and Bunds reached extreme bearish levels at end of September. GS CFTC data shows managed money deeply net short US Treasuries. A pause in yields could force short covering and a bond bounce.
Trend followers were the standout strategy of 2026 (+15.7% over 9M per SG CTA Index), mainly from bond shorts and oil longs.
KOSPI has lost momentum, opening a short-term divergence versus the SOX while investors have recently loaded up on SOX exposure.

GS reports speculative silver positioning deteriorated sharply: Managed Money, Other and Non-Reportable traders sold a combined $1.6bn in the final week of September, the largest weekly selling since February, split evenly between long liquidation ($800mn) and fresh shorts ($800mn).

Silver vol has reset from around 37 up to a peak of 110 and is back near where it started, but 25-delta put-call skew has richened into its top decile over two years, so downside protection remains expensive.
